title: OpenAI responses v5 compatibility: seed/idempotency shim + structured tool-call passthrough
author: Priya Kothari
description: Context and motivation: Responses v5 introduced a small-but-important set of fields commonly used by customers migrating from OpenAI: a top-level `seed_hint` / `deterministic` pair for repeatability, and a `metadata` object that must be passed through verbatim into the final tool/function call payload and the recorded response for auditability. Our hosted API previously supported older 'seed' semantics (internal deterministic RNG flag) and ad-hoc metadata propagation for a subset of tool calls. This PR adds a compatibility shim so v5 OpenAI-style requests are honored without requiring changes to the runtime kernel.
commits: a1f2b3c: compat: map responses-v5 seed_hint -> runtime seed_id + idempotency header
b2c3d4e: api: preserve metadata blob and attach to ToolCall.payload under 'client_metadata'
c3d4e5f: runtime: ensure deterministic RNG toggle applied to streaming segments and KV cache reattach
d4e5f6a: sdk-python: add ResponsesV5Request wrapper and example migration guide
e5f6a7b: tests: integration tests for streaming + seed reassembly and concurrency edge cases
review_comments: André: Can you clarify how seed_hint interacts with batched requests? We need to avoid cross-request leakage when batching mixes deterministic and non-deterministic requests.

Author (Priya): Seed_hint is materialized as a per-request seed_id and we add it to the batching key. Batches will be segmented by seed_id so deterministic requests are never co-batched with others; documented in runtime/streaming/reassembly.go. See new unit test 'BatchSegmentationBySeed' added in mapping_test.go.
Maya: Test flakiness observed in reassembly test on CI (timeout). Suggest reducing timeout and adding a backoff retry for streaming chunk ordering guarantees.
Author (Priya): Reduced test timeouts and added a deterministic scheduler stub for the integration test to eliminate CI timing flakiness. Also added an explicit assertion on chunk sequence numbers.
Jordan: SDK change looks good. Please include a short example in docs showing how metadata is surfaced in function/tool outputs (audit use-case).
Author (Priya): Added docs/migration/openai_v5_migration.md with an example mapping metadata->client_metadata and a note about audit logging retention.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash. Rollout: staged canary on dedicated regions for 24h, then full main rollout. No rollback required during canary. DB migration: none.
release_notes: Adds OpenAI Responses v5 compatibility shim: maps seed_hint/deterministic to runtime seed_id, ensures deterministic requests are batched separately, preserves top-level metadata into tool/function call payloads and audit logs. Includes SDK Python wrapper and migration docs. Backwards compatible with existing OpenAI/Redwood requests.
notes_and_migration: Operational notes: 1) Deterministic requests are isolated at batching boundary — expect slightly higher per-token cost for deterministic-heavy traffic because of reduced batching efficiency. 2) Metadata is stored verbatim for audit; large metadata blobs (>32KB) are rejected with a 400 and guidance to use object storage references. 3) SDK and examples updated; customers migrating should test critical prompt sets with the Responses v5 flag and verify seed-based repeats in staging before enabling in prod.
test_matrix_summary: Unit tests added for mapping and batch segmentation. Integration matrix covers streaming reassembly, concurrency with mixed deterministic flags, and metadata passthrough for function/tool calls. Manual QA ran end-to-end with a sample tool that returns structured JSON and verified schema integrity after passthrough.
additional_context: This change is intentionally implemented as a compatibility layer in services/openai-compat to keep the core runtime stable. Future work (ENG-4250) will consolidate seeding APIs and expose a first-class deterministic mode in the public Redwood API.
